response.evidence: Analysis of the dataset shows 1,000 loan records with 11 denials specifically for Black or African American applicants out of approximately 40 total applicants in this demographic group (27.5% denial rate). Comparing across racial groups: White applicants show ~6.5% denial rate, Hispanic/Latino ~8%, and Asian ~6%. While Black/African American applicants have a higher denial rate, this alone does not conclusively prove discrimination without examining the underlying financial criteria. The Black/African American applicants denied included cases with: high debt-to-income ratios (50%-60%), high loan-to-value ratios (90-100%), and other risk factors consistent with denial patterns across other groups. However, the elevated denial rate (27.5% vs 6-8% for other groups) warrants concern and would require further investigation into whether differences in approved loan characteristics (income, debt ratios, credit factors not in this dataset) account for the disparity, or if bias in application of lending standards occurred.
